mappings.note: What the birds' life teaches us -- the poem's usefulness, gathered as a set of lessons. Rejected LO-118: what we take from it, not one idea of the poet's.
Whom the poet addresses as 'jag ke bandi maanav' AND why -- his idea about self-made bonds. Rejected LO-124, kept for the item that only glosses the phrase.
The poem's central feeling -- its usefulness stated whole. Rejected LO-118: the message, not his handling.
Why the poet counsels breaking the fetter on one's foot -- his reasoning about freedom lost to grief and greed. Rejected LO-124, kept for the gloss of 'bedi pag mein'.
How the birds behave to one another -- stated in the poem. Rejected LO-118: no inference.
What the birds' working all day MEANS -- keyed as constant effort for food, an interpretation. Rejected LO-121, used for the bare 'who works all day' item.
What kind of self-reliance the birds have -- feeding themselves and building their own nests, drawn out from the poem. Rejected LO-121: the term is the reader's.
Sense of the line 'unke man mein lobh nahin hai' -- the gloss of 'lobh' and what it rules out. Rejected LO-118: a phrase, not a proposition.
What the line about flying in the boundless sky teaches -- reading the poet's claim about breaking needless bonds. Rejected LO-121: the lesson is inferred.
What the chidiya says to us in the prem-preeti line -- the poet's idea. Rejected LO-124, kept for the gloss item.
Explicate the line about not wanting to seize the world's wealth -- the poet's claim about contentment. Rejected LO-124: a whole line's argument.
Sense of 'paap nahin parvaah nahin' -- two short words to be glossed. Rejected LO-118: the words carry it.
Explicate the line about living and eating together -- keyed as equality and unity, a reading past the words. Rejected LO-121: the line states the fact, not the value.
How the song strikes the POET and what he thinks -- his response, which the poem shows rather than states. Rejected LO-121 for that reason.
Which marks of the birds the poem names -- a catalogue gathered by close reading. Rejected LO-120: an inventory, not the message.
What the poet means to say through 'sone ki kadiyaan todo' -- his message about material bonds. Rejected LO-124, used where only the phrase is glossed.
How the chidiya's conduct can inspire man -- the poem's usefulness. Rejected LO-118: what we take from it.

What attitude we should hold towards nature and living creatures -- the key argues co-existence and not destroying their habitats, which is the learner's reasoned response to a natural-world issue. Rejected LO-120: the answer goes past the poem.
Why man is called 'bedi pag mein' -- unpacking that figure. Rejected LO-118, kept for the item asking why the poet counsels breaking it.
Why the birds compare themselves with man -- the poet's purpose in the comparison. Rejected LO-121: no line states it.
What the closing actions -- sitting, singing, flying off -- convey. Reading the poet's design. Rejected LO-121: the actions are stated, the message is not.

Birds are dwindling: what would YOU suggest to stop it. The key reasons from pollution, felling and noise to concrete measures -- the learner's own reasoned response to a local natural issue, which is exactly this outcome. Rejected LO-120: nothing in the poem answers it.
Explain 'droh-bhaavna' against humanity as used in that line -- the coinage is the demand. Rejected LO-118, kept for the item asking what the chidiya means by the whole line.
What inspiration the prem-preeti line gives -- what we take from it. Rejected LO-118, used where the item asks what she says rather than what we gain.
What the boundless-sky line teaches -- the poet's claim about fearless freedom. Rejected LO-121: inferred, not stated.
Which moral and life lessons the poem gives through the chidiya, in detail -- its usefulness. Rejected LO-118: the whole yield of the poem.

The relation between nature and the birds AND the message for man -- the key argues interdependence and co-existence past what the poem says. Rejected LO-118: the reasoning is about the natural world, not only the poet's idea.
The purport of the mukti-mantra line, which bonds hold man, and which release she points to -- the poet's argument in full. Rejected LO-124: more than a gloss is wanted.
What the chidiya urges man to learn at the poem's close, and why -- his reasoning. Rejected LO-120: his argument rather than the poem's use.
The poem's root feeling and, in your own words, the poet's message -- the text's usefulness. Rejected LO-126: the demand is the message, not a piece of the learner's own experience.
Describe man's limits and the birds' freedom, then say which way the poet leans and why -- weighing the poet's position. Rejected LO-119: no preference of the learner's is being argued.

How man complicates his own life by moving away from natural living -- the key reasons about material pursuit and stress beyond the poem, a response to a real condition. Rejected LO-118: the argument is the learner's to build.

How birds live collectively beyond boundaries while man is bound -- the key names the walls of caste, religion, house and wealth that man has raised. Caste and religion are named in this outcome among the sensitive issues on which a learner should reason, so this is its proper home. Rejected LO-118: the subject becomes social division, not the poet's figure.
Who 've' are in the quoted line (the birds) -- pronoun reference located in the extract. Rejected LO-118: no idea weighed.
Who are 'svachchhand' (the birds) -- located in the extract. Rejected LO-124: the word is quoted, not glossed.
Who sings a while on the peepal (the chidiya). Rejected LO-115: a fact, not a rendering.
What the birds teach man -- to live together and freely, a reading of the poem's point. Rejected LO-121: no line states it.
Purport of 'we are free, why have you put a fetter on your foot' -- the poet's contrast. Rejected LO-124, kept for the item glossing 'bedi pag mein'.
Of whom the absence of greed is said (the birds) -- located in the extract. Rejected LO-118: attribution.
What the birds feel with what their labour brings (contentment) -- located in the extract. Rejected LO-118: stated.
